exposure: maternal hypotension (SBP<100 mmHg or DBP<60 mmHg)
uterine hyperstimulation (prolonged contractions for over 2 minutes)
outcome: prolonged deceleration (lasting more than 3 minutes) after neuraxial analgesia (PDAA)
cohort: The study included 898 singleton term pregnant women who underwent neuraxial analgesia during labor.
finding: Uterine hyperstimulation, nulliparity, and higher pre-analgesia pain intensity were independently associated with prolonged deceleration after neuraxial analgesia (PDAA), with uterine hyperstimulation being the strongest factor, while post-analgesia hypotension was not a key factor.
